For God works through the hands of saints to bring about His glory; if His Spirit glorifies the Son, how can one speaking in the Spirit speak ill of Him?; those who attribute creation to someone other than the One through whom all things came into being would be completely without the Holy Spirit; they explicitly say 'Anathema Jesus'; those who confess Jesus as God and Lord will be rightly guided by the Spirit; the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God, and conveys this knowledge to the saints; Paul testifies to this, saying there are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit; and different kinds of service, but the same Lord; and different kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all; just as earthly rulers reward their loyal servants with various honors, so the Holy Trinity distributes the gifts of heavenly goods to those who love it with a pure heart and mind, through the Spirit, as through Christ, from the Father; all things are given from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit; each person is given the manifestation of the Spirit for their benefit; to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit...

For He knows the suitable times for each of the things done by Him, in which all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden, according to what is written. What kinds of gifts and what kinds of distributions, and also the workings of powers, are made clear by saying that to one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit. The word of wisdom is, in my opinion, the one that is in the opening of the mouth, prompt, and easy, and as if going from a very fluent tongue. To another is given the word of knowledge. For there are some among us who do not have what is prompt for words, and are not able to speak easily with boldness, but are very deep in understanding, most intelligent, and very weak in speaking the sacred words, and are able to initiate others and easily interpret the things that have been contemplated. But the word of wisdom and also of knowledge is distributed through one Spirit to those who are worthy, from the Father through the Son. The word of knowledge is when someone knows the mind of the divine sayings and is able to unfold thoughts, but is not able to teach these things easily. And this and that are distributed through one Spirit to those who are worthy, from the Father through the Son, who is said to distribute the services. For to some of the holy apostles, He commanded to proclaim the word of faith to those from the blood of Israel. And to others, He assigned the lands of the Gentiles. And this was worked through the Holy Spirit.

And indeed in the acts of the holy apostles it will be found written that while they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them'; and the divine Paul is appointed to the apostleship of the nations, and he obtained this ministry; and he himself writes and says, 'As long as I am an apostle of the nations, I glorify my ministry'; therefore the Son distributes the ministries, and the Holy Spirit effects the thing with authority; for the Spirit is of the Son; but also the workings of the powers, that is
pass_b_english: God works through the hands of saints to bring about His glory, and it is through His Spirit that He accomplishes this.
If the Spirit of God glorifies the Son, it is impossible for someone speaking in the Spirit to speak ill of Him.
On the other hand, those who attribute creation to someone other than the One through whom all things came into being would be completely without the Holy Spirit.
They explicitly say 'Anathema Jesus'.
In contrast, those who confess Jesus as God and Lord will be rightly guided by the Spirit, who searches all things, even the depths of God, and conveys this knowledge to the saints.

The apostle Paul testifies to this, saying that there are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit, and different kinds of service, but the same Lord, and different kinds of workings, but the same God who works all things in all (1 Corinthians 12:4-6).

Just as earthly rulers reward their loyal servants with various honors, so the Holy Trinity distributes the gifts of heavenly goods to those who love it with a pure heart and mind, through the Spirit, as through Christ, from the Father.
All things are given from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit, and each person is given the manifestation of the Spirit for their benefit.
God knows the suitable times for each of the things He does, and all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden in Him, as it is written (Colossians 2:3).
To one is given the word of wisdom through the Spirit.
In my opinion, the word of wisdom is the one that flows easily from a very fluent tongue, and it is characterized by being prompt and effortless.
To another person, the Spirit gives the word of knowledge.
There are some people who may not be able to speak easily or with boldness, but they are very deep in understanding and have a profound grasp of the sacred words.
They may not be able to teach others easily, but they are able to initiate them into the mysteries and interpret the things that have been contemplated.
The word of wisdom and the word of knowledge are both distributed by the one Spirit to those who are worthy, from the Father through the Son.
For to some of the holy apostles, He commanded to proclaim the word of faith to those from the blood of Israel, and to others, He assigned the lands of the Gentiles.

And indeed in the acts of the holy apostles it will be found written that while they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them' (Acts 13:2).

This marked the beginning of Paul's apostleship to the nations, a ministry that he would later glorify in his writings, saying 'As long as I am an apostle of the nations, I glorify my ministry' (Romans 11:13).
Therefore, the Son distributes the ministries, and the Holy Spirit effects the thing with authority; for the Spirit is of the Son.
Thus, those who attribute creation to someone other than the One through whom all things came into being would be completely without the Holy Spirit, for they are not rightly guided by the Spirit.
